4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your published bug report (the GitHub Issue you filed on your partner's ROLLER repo) plus your Bug Fix Report on your portfolio site — 1 bug in your own game (filed by a classmate, or found yourself) documented, fixed with Copilot, tested by you as QA, and signed off, with ROLLER v2 pushed. Monday the class votes on its top 3 games, and the winners get played on DONUTS Tuesday.
4th Period.workingNow: Filing the bug you found as a GitHub Issue on your partner's repo — with detailed steps and screenshots.
4th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, I can file 1 GitHub Issue on my partner's repo with a clear title, numbered steps, expected vs. actual, and at least 2 screenshots, so they can find and fix the bug without asking me anything.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.19 — Document programs in order to make them easier to follow, test, and debug.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.2 — Interacting with others in written English in various communicative forms.
agenda: Overview: why detail beats "it's broken" (3 min)
I do: file a bug Issue with screenshots, live (12 min)
We do: check one Issue against the checklist (7 min)
You do: file your bug Issue with 2+ screenshots (18 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your Issue link (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you found a bug in your partner's mod. A bug nobody can find again never gets fixed, so today is all about the report: a [BUG] title, numbered steps, what should happen vs. what did, and screenshots that show it. Thursday you switch sides and fix the bug someone filed on YOU.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your finished game, published and embedded on your Google Site, plus your Fix Your Bug sheet — 1 bug (from your tester, or found yourself) written down, fixed with Perplexity, tested by you, and 3 sentences on what you changed and why. Monday the class votes on its top 3 games, and the winners get played on DONUTS Tuesday.
6th Period.workingNow: Swapping roles: watching someone else play your game and writing down what you see.
6th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, I can watch a partner play my game without giving hints and fill in both my tester notes and my observer notes, so I know what to fix.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.15 — Seek and incorporate feedback from team members and users to refine a solution that meets user needs.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.5 — Listening actively to spoken English in a range of social and academic contexts.
agenda: Review: tester vs. creator — creator stays quiet (5 min)
I do: what good observer notes look like (5 min)
Swap playtest: watch your game get played (20 min)
Finish your tester and observer notes (10 min)
Exit Ticket: one surprise from watching (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday you were the tester and found a bug in someone else's game. Today you switch: someone plays YOUR game while you watch quietly and write down every place they get stuck. Seeing a real player struggle is how creators learn what to fix. Thursday you fix it.
